description.value:
Cryptidkin.

“Every settlement has a story about you. None of them are accurate. All of them are useful.”

Cryptidkin Core Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (set by subspecies).

  • Speed. 6 squares (subspecies may override).

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Cryptidkin does not grant fixed bonuses. Subspecies lean expressed through Tier powers.

Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

Wasteland Adapted. You reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison. You ignore the first nonmagical environmental hazard you encounter each turn (heat, cold, radiation taint, wind shear, fume pockets).

Survivor’s Instinct. When you roll initiative, you can choose to know the position of the nearest exit, the nearest threat, or the nearest ally within 12 squares You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Subspecies. Choose one Cryptidkin subspecies (Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin). Your subspecies grants Tier powers as you level (Tier I at creation, then 5/11/17).

advancement.hint: Gain the core Cryptidkin ancestry traits.

description.value:
Cryptidkin Subspecies. This heritage preserves the original UUID for Jackalope (Bad Eden) while converting it from a species-root to a Cryptidkin subspecies.

“You don’t spot a Jackalope. You notice the world flinch, and then realize why.”

Jackalope. Fast because they have to be. Twitchy because the world has trained them that stillness is how you die. Half-remembered pre-Shattering folklore, half radiation-assembled rumor, and fully people.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium.

  • Speed. 7 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. Your subspecies leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Jackalope Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Jackalope powers emphasize: Startle Reflex (can’t-be-caught-flat burst), Wasteland Bound (long-distance run), Horns of Bad Luck (jinx aura), Can’t Catch Me (evasion), and strategic Bad Omen Runner Domain hooks.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

If you see Jackalope tracks circling your hex, you are not under attack. You are being advised.

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +10 Soft Power marks and +10 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

  • Trail Whisper. Once per turn, your Domain can reroll a single Travel or Scout check made in a hex adjacent to your home territory.

description.value:
"You aren't fast because you're fast. You're fast because the world keeps deciding to miss."

Startle Reflex (1/Soma Break). Reaction when you are targeted by an attack roll or fail an Intrigue check — move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

Horns of Bad Luck. Your natural horns ship as a Jackalope-only Manifestation when you take the heritage — see your Manifestations tab. When violence escalates around you, the GM may describe unsettling omens tied to your presence — a mirror crack, a dropped knife, a candle going out the wrong direction.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Startle Reflex Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Reaction  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. When targeted by an attack roll or you fail an Intrigue check, move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

"You're already moving. The fight rearranges around it."

The Shadow Courier runs on Surge, like everyone — but yours comes from motion. Move 30+ ft in a turn and you bank +1 Surge (again at 12 squares, max +2/round). A courier in motion has options; a courier standing still is just a target. The old Pace pool folds into this — same fuel, one number.

The Courier (spent via Surge)

  • Courier's Step (1) — +half-speed move (no provoke) and a freed reaction; flow through the fight.
  • Ghoststep (3) — DR equal to Tier till your next turn, and reposition out of danger.
  • Flank & Strike (5) — reposition, then your next Strike reroll the lowest die and +Tier d6.
  • No Such Door (8) — allies within Tier squares each gain a freed reaction and a reroll; open the road for the whole team.

The Package endures as your work — designate it, carry it, deliver it. Delivery banks your Surge to full and still triggers the route's strategic payoff (Intrigue marks, Darkness reduction, the arrival that mattered).

description.value:
A locked door is a suggestion.

Mode: Thief / drift: Toward.

Your default Package type is either a Blade or a Key. Declare which you are carrying at the start of each scene; you may switch on a Soma Break.

  • Blade. A single opportunistic strike, deployable once. While carrying a Blade, your first attack from concealment or surprise in the scene deals an extra +1d10 kinetic damage with (blade). The damage explodes on 10s and banks Surge as normal. Using the strike consumes the Blade.

  • Key. A single-use access bypass. While carrying a Key, you may bypass one non-magical lock, ward, or password challenge without rolling, once per scene. Using the Key consumes it.

On delivery (resolving the Blade strike on its intended target, or using the Key on its intended barrier): — see Class Tier 3 Package Mastery for the Black Stair delivery bonus.

You may designate a new Package on your next Soma Break or on entering a new scene if your slot is empty.

description.value:
You cross what isn't supposed to be crossed — and you always come out the other side carrying something.

On gaining Shadow Courier Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Stealth (Intrigue).

  • Skill rank +1 in Tinkering (Intrigue).

  • +20 Intrigue marks and +20 Logistics marks to your Domain's caps.

  • You bank Surge by moving: 6 squares on your turn banks +1, again at 12 (max +2 a round).

  • Package slot comes online — one Package at a time, type set by your chosen Route at L1.

Spend Surge from the ◆ Surge menu: Snap Strike, Flank & Strike, Clear Road, Quiet Voyage and your Route's spends.

Liminal Sense. Once a scene, ignore the first detection-style roll an opponent attempts against you (perception, scrying, Insight to read your intent, etc.). The roll is treated as if it had failed; resources spent on the attempt are not refunded.

system.source: Bad Eden Originals — Sprint F (2026 rules)

description.value:
"You came through a door that wasn't for them."

Doctrine: Thresholds weaponized — covert, predatory; who gets through and who really, really doesn't.

The Black Stair is the courier as ambush. Your Surge spends turn crossings into kills: strike from where they weren't watching, slam the threshold shut on a foe, and spring the stair that does not end.

Route (spent via Surge)

  • Ambush (1) — your next Strike +Tier d6; the target's next attack is rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.

  • Cut Off (2) — a foe is Staggered and cannot take reactions until your next turn.

  • Stair-Trap (5) — your next Strike lands as a max-die crit and knocks the target Prone; if it drops them, you regain a freed action.

"You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a story the world made into a person because it needed you in the room."

Folklore Presence. 1/Soma Break, when you first meet a community, decide whether the rumors about you arrived first. If yes, reroll the lowest die on your first Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check with anyone in that community (your choice which skill, declared when you roll). The rumor is not always flattering — the GM gets to colour it.

Wasteland Adapted. Reroll the lowest die on defense checks against disease and environmental poison. You can subsist on rations that would sicken most humans (spoiled meat, swamp water, mushroom flesh).

Survivor's Instinct. 1/Soma Break, when you would drop to 0 Integrity, you may instead drop to 1 Integrity and gain one level of Stress.

items.name: Black Stair L5: The Threshold Is A Lie

description.value:
Wards aren't walls. They're paperwork.

When you use your class's The Crossing ability (Class Tier 2) on a magical barrier, treat the barrier's check DC as if it were 2 lower.

Additionally, you leave no magical trace of the crossing — divination cast after the fact does not reveal that you passed, no alarm aftermath fires, no scrying residue lingers — unless the barrier was specifically warded against your character or class. Most weren't, because most wardmakers don't know you exist.

If a barrier is specifically warded against you, the DC reduction still applies, but the no-trace effect does not.

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, the membrane chooses you instead of the wall.

The Crossing — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As an action, declare a single threshold within reach: a door, wall, ward, alarm, divination perimeter, hex boundary, or similar barrier. You cross it. Resolution depends on the barrier:

  • Mundane barriers (locked doors, sealed walls, alarmed corridors, password gates) simply fail to register your passage. No roll. The barrier remains intact for everyone else.

  • Magical wards or alarms (alarm manifestations, divination perimeters, scrying screens, hex-warded boundaries) require an Intrigue defense check against DC 12 + (the ward source's Initiation tier × 2). On a success you cross without triggering the ward; on a failure you still cross, but the ward fires normally and the source is alerted.

The Black Stair's L5 feature extends The Crossing.

Calculated Risk

You open yourself on purpose.

Rules

Once per turn, you may choose to reroll the lowest die on an attack roll. If you do, attack rolls against you reroll the lowest die until the start of your next turn.

🃏 Card — once per turn: banks a reroll for your attack; attacks against you reroll their lowest die until your next turn (GM applies).

description.value:
What you carry, no one else can find.

When you take a non-owned object, a piece of information, or a willing small creature into your possession as a Package, both you and the Package become untraceable by divination:

  • Scrying, Locate Object, Locate Creature, Detect Thoughts, and equivalent divinatory effects all fail against you for the duration.

  • Scent-tracking, magical mark-tracking, and faction-loyalty tracking all lose your trail at the moment of extraction.

The protection holds until any of these occur:

  • You deliver the Package to its intended destination.

  • You willingly reveal your location or the Package's location.

  • 24 hours pass.

You may carry a non-Package object as a Package for the purpose of this feature only — the Package slot is occupied even if no doctrine effect applies to the contents.
